markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a controlled sampling experiment within the supplied BERT4Rec. The supplied historical score, 0.5825, does not establish a treatment effect because paired control results are absent.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, recent-prefix supervision could help distinguish present preferences from broad associations. This directly targets the simulator’s complaint that plausible but weak matches displace specific choices. Second, strictly truncated prefixes teach next-choice prediction without exposing future events. They may reduce reliance on stale purchases, although recency alone cannot identify completed needs. Third, separately normalized reconstruction and terminal losses make their coefficients interpretable. Missing training counters mean diagnostic terminal coverage cannot verify this balance.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec [1] supplies the compatible masked bidirectional backbone. Its reconstruction objective motivates retaining masked learning while testing terminal supervision. TiSASRec [2] distinguishes elapsed time from event position. This cautions against interpreting recent-ten sampling as temporal modeling. gSASRec [3] motivates examining negative-sampling overconfidence. It supports an objective-focused alternative, without proving that harder negatives solve the measured errors.

The framework has three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision allocation | Recent nonterminal cutoffs | Context length and item exposure also change |
| Temporal representation | Learned event-distance attention bias | Recency can reinforce completed purchases |
| Discrimination objective | Moderately hard negatives from the same network | Unobserved positives may be penalized |

Scores below use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell includes a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Endpoint-preserving recent cutoffs [1,2] | 3: clear ablation; established ingredients | 6: useful evidence; exposure confounding | 7: targets specificity/staleness; no need inference | 6: terminal discrimination; causal link unproven | 3: sampler change; bookkeeping required |
| Learned distance attention bias [2] | 4: BERT adaptation; familiar mechanism | 7: adaptive recency; added tuning | 6: context sensitivity; no compatibility evidence | 5: richer features; concentration may persist | 6: internal bias; predictor synchronization |
| Mixed uniform/moderately hard negatives [3] | 3: focused objective; established approach | 6: stronger competition; false negatives | 5: sharper ranking; relevance uncertain | 7: targets negative margins; probes use sampled pairs | 5: shared network; mining costs |

**Selected experiment.** Compare uniform nonterminal cutoffs against an equal uniform/recent-ten mixture, fixing full-history endpoint probability at 0.1. Both retain equal, separately normalized reconstruction and terminal losses. This explicitly targets broad associations outranking current preferences and stale purchases implying continuing demand. It also targets weak discrimination: negative-beats-positive rates are 11.49% and 12.42% in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics. These observations motivate testing; they predict no gain.

Use one independently trained model per category in each separate trial. Select solely through pinned macro validation HR@10; preserve seeds, limits, routing, diagnostics and predictor consistency. Log endpoint exceptions, actual branch allocation, context lengths and target frequencies. Compatibility, quantity suitability and unresolved needs remain unobserved.

idea.description: Run a controlled, endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff sampling experiment in the corrected BERT4Rec. Compare a uniform-cutoff control with a treatment that mixes uniform and recent-ten nonterminal targets equally. Each trial trains exactly one model per category; predictions never combine trials or independently fitted components.
idea.motivation: The proposal addresses two reported user failures: broad associations displacing specific current preferences, and historical purchases being interpreted as continuing demand. Strict-prefix terminal supervision may teach more context-specific next-choice discrimination. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile sampled training margins, −0.1487 and −0.2356, which motivate testing this discrimination hypothesis. Neither these probes nor the supplied historical score establish a validation improvement or prove that recency resolves completed needs.
idea.implementation_notes:
Establish the uniform control before testing treatment; do not assume that prior repeated descriptions establish this comparison. Preserve the corrected BERT4Rec architecture, optimizer, reconstruction masking, user sampling and checkpoint-selection protocol. Optimize 0.5 times mean reconstruction target CE plus 0.5 times mean terminal target CE, with both branches nonempty under a common eligibility rule. Terminal examples contain only events preceding the selected target occurrence, followed by the reserved MASK; exclude all subsequent events. Earlier occurrences of the same item remain valid history. Reconstruction retains the corrected masked-target policy and never uses shifted labels visible through bidirectional input.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Retain all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], fixed splits, single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. All trials, diagnostics and failures count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Use the same predetermined checkpoint-selection rule in both arms; deploy one checkpoint per category without averaging or score fusion.

For both arms, derive independent data RNG streams with NumPy SeedSequence([42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]), using the documented category order and fixed integer purpose IDs. Separate user sampling, cutoff uniforms, reconstruction masks and negative sampling; keep model initialization/dropout RNG separate. Match user batches and cutoff uniforms across arms, acknowledging that this stream scheme changes baseline draws and does not guarantee identical realized corruption or hardware-level determinism.

Skip histories shorter than two events. Histories with exactly two events have one eligible target, so select the endpoint with probability one and record the exception. For longer histories, endpoint probability is exactly 0.1; conditional nonterminal probabilities are uniform in control and a 0.5 uniform/0.5 recent-ten mixture in treatment. This is event-position recency, not elapsed-time decay.

Persist measured per-epoch and cumulative branch counts, valid target counts, coefficient masses, target-weighted CE, endpoint/singleton/skipped counts, target-frequency distributions, context-length histograms and timing. Coefficient mass is neither loss-value share nor gradient share. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual view.model and the ModelView compatibility interfaces. Diagnostic-loader coverage cannot recover missing training allocation. Read the maximum nonpadding index in left-padded sequences, never count minus one. Keep appended-MASK inference and the embedded predictor writer consistent; this sampler-only intervention requires no inference architecture change.

Select through the unchanged host macro validation HR@10. If host per-user hits are available, report gained/lost hits and a paired, category-stratified bootstrap interval; otherwise omit such uncertainty estimates. Do not invent metrics. Probe the same twenty training users for specific-choice judgments and duplication/staleness rejection reasons using unseen full-catalog recommendations. Use histories, titles, descriptions and observed timestamps only. Treat unidentified suitability as uncertain. Context length and target frequency are mediators of the policy effect, so the main comparison cannot isolate recency alone.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

CATEGORIES = ('Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
              'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl')

def data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]))

def choose_target(history, u, treatment):
    n = len(history)
    if n < 2:
        return None, 'skipped'
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    m = n - 2  # eligible nonterminal indices: 1 through n-2
    probabilities = np.full(m, 1.0 / m)
    if treatment:
        k = min(10, m)
        probabilities *= 0.5
        probabilities[-k:] += 0.5 / k
    cdf = np.cumsum(probabilities)
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    index = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1)
    return index + 1, 'nonterminal'

originality.positive: The fixed endpoint probability and independently normalized branches define a precise, interpretable BERT4Rec sampling ablation.
originality.negative: Recent-target weighting and strict-prefix prediction are established ingredients; this is a controlled refinement rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: A feasible early experiment can determine whether changing terminal target exposure merits further temporal modeling under this benchmark.
future_potential.negative: The total policy effect mixes event recency, context length and item frequency, while current need and compatibility remain unobserved.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention changes sampling while preserving the backbone, checkpoint format and inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable comparison still requires matched random streams, explicit short-history handling, persistent counters and budget accounting.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the bidirectional masked-item modeling foundation retained by every proposed experiment.
Motivates learning from masked contexts while predicting through an appended mask at inference.
limitations: Does not establish the effect of the proposed endpoint-preserving cutoff distribution on the pinned four-category benchmark.
Masked reconstruction alone does not explicitly identify current needs or completed purchases.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models interaction intervals alongside sequence positions.
Provides motivation for distinguishing elapsed time from event-position recency.
limitations: Its backbone is not the required BERT4Rec backbone; only its temporal ideas are relevant here.
Does not validate recent-ten cutoff sampling or prove that recent purchases imply continuing demand.

related_work.title: gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract)
contributions: Links sparse negative sampling to overconfidence in sequential recommendation.
Motivates a later objective-level experiment within the retained BERT4Rec network.
limitations: Does not establish that hard-negative mining improves this benchmark.
Sampling-objective changes cannot independently identify false negatives or resolve item suitability.
